reasoning: Recent general‑election polling aggregates show Democrats with a very large advantage in the Massachusetts Senate race, with Ed Markey leading the likely Republican nominee John Deaton by roughly the low‑20s in margin (about D+23), while no fresh state‑level general‑election presidential polling appeared in the last 45 days; structurally and historically, the state leans strongly Democratic at the presidential level as well.[2] Within the last 45 days, all public polling and coverage has focused on the *Democratic primary* between Markey and Seth Moulton, where multiple high‑quality polls consistently show Markey ahead by mid‑ to high‑double‑digit margins (roughly D+14 to D+28 among Democratic primary voters).[1][4][5][7][8][9][13] Cook’s statewide PVI continues to rate Massachusetts as a solidly Democratic state (about D+12), reinforcing that even absent fresh presidential general‑election polls, both the Senate and presidential contests currently favor Democrats by substantial margins.[10][12][15]

sources.name: Pollsmax – 2026 Massachusetts Senate Polling Average
sources.details: Pollsmax’s Massachusetts Senate polling average, based on seven recent general‑election polls including a June 23 UNH survey, shows Ed Markey at 54.1% vs. John Deaton at 31.0%, a D+23.1 margin.

sources.name: UMass Amherst/WCVB – Democratic Senate Primary Poll (reported by WBUR)
sources.details: A UMass Amherst/WCVB poll of 445 likely Democratic primary voters finds Markey leading Moulton 60% to 32% in the Democratic Senate primary, a 28‑point margin.

sources.name: Boston Herald – UMass Amherst/WCVB Democratic Senate Primary Poll
sources.details: Coverage of the same UMass Amherst/WCVB poll emphasizes that Markey’s lead over Moulton has grown to nearly 30 points, with toplines of 60% Markey vs. 32% Moulton among Democratic and independent primary voters.

sources.name: WGBH – UMass Amherst/WCVB Democratic Senate Primary Poll
sources.details: WGBH’s write‑up of the UMass Amherst/WCVB survey notes that Markey holds a 28‑point lead over Moulton, 60% to 32%, among Democratic primary voters statewide.

sources.name: Axios Boston – UMass Amherst/WCVB YouGov Democratic Senate Primary Poll
sources.details: Axios Boston reports on the UMass Amherst/WCVB YouGov poll, highlighting Markey’s 60% to 32% lead over Moulton (D+28) and describing his position as a commanding advantage across demographic groups.

sources.name: Boston.com – UMass Amherst/WCVB Democratic Senate Primary Poll
sources.details: Boston.com’s coverage of the UMass Amherst/WCVB poll similarly reports Markey at 60% versus Moulton at 32% among Democratic primary voters, framing the race as Markey in a strong position heading into the primary.

sources.name: Suffolk University/Boston Globe – Democratic Senate Primary Poll
sources.details: A Suffolk University/Boston Globe poll of 500 likely Democratic primary voters finds Markey at 52.2% and Moulton at roughly 38%, a lead of just over 14 percentage points, with about 9% undecided.

sources.name: PredictionHunt – July Democratic Senate Primary Poll Summary
sources.details: PredictionHunt summarizes a July survey showing Markey leading Moulton 41% to 35% in the Democratic Senate primary (D+6), noting that his advantage had narrowed compared with earlier polling and that undecided voters had grown to about 23%.

sources.name: PredictionHunt – UNH Democratic Senate Primary Poll (June)
sources.details: Another PredictionHunt piece cites a UNH Survey Center poll conducted June 18-23 putting Markey at 41% and Moulton at 35% among likely Democratic primary voters, a 6‑point advantage, while emphasizing that roughly 24% remained undecided.

sources.name: PredictionEdge – Massachusetts Republican Senate Primary Odds
sources.details: PredictionEdge tracks odds and limited data around the Massachusetts Republican Senate primary, indicating John Deaton as an overwhelming favorite over intra‑party rivals, but without general‑election head‑to‑head numbers versus Markey.

sources.name: Ballotpedia – 2026 U.S. Senate Election in Massachusetts Overview
sources.details: Ballotpedia’s overview of the 2026 U.S. Senate election in Massachusetts describes rating categories and notes that mainstream forecasters typically assign Massachusetts Senate races to Democratic‑favored categories such as "Likely" or "Safe" given the state’s partisan lean, though it does not quote a specific numeric margin.

sources.name: Cook Political Report – Partisan Voting Index (Massachusetts)
sources.details: Cook Political Report’s PVI map and associated materials list Massachusetts as a strongly Democratic state, with a statewide Partisan Voting Index of about D+12 relative to the national average, indicating a structural advantage for Democrats in both Senate and presidential races.
